correctness.rationale: The difference recurrence repeats a length-three block; if 3 does not divide n only the zero periodic solution is possible. For n=3k, toggling a nonzero kernel pattern, e.g. (110)^k, is admissible exactly when each block of the source is independently 100 or 010. Thus each of the three nonzero differences yields 2^(k−1) unordered pairs. Two such admissibility classes intersect only at the corresponding constant choice of a one-site phase, so only the three period-three sources have two distinct partners. They all produce 1^n; its fourth full-shift predecessor is 1^n itself, inadmissible. Counting pairs and total sources (the Lucas trace) proves all positive fiber counts and the claimed image size. The unique-recovery fraction and exponential estimate then follow. At n=1 and 2 the literal three-XOR rule is the identity and the source counts are 1 and 3. Independent enumeration through n=18 reproduced the source and fiber counts, including the triple, as finite corroboration.
residual_risks: For 3 dividing n, four full-shift preimages refers to attainable outputs; other outputs have zero. Finite enumeration is not the proof for all n.
